subject: Coordinating a technical deep-dive across US / EU / APAC — proposed "timeband" approach
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@strata.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: technical deep-dive with architects across US/EU/APAC

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — we want to follow up with a deeper technical session with our architecture leads in the US, EU and APAC. Goal: walk through the integration patterns (VPC, private deploy), performance SLOs, and a live troubleshooting of our sample workload.

Attendees likely to join: Sophie Li (EU infra architect), Kenji Nakamura (APAC infra lead), myself (US). Sophie prefers late morning CET, Kenji prefers morning JST, and I am flexible between 07:00–11:00 EST.

Can Redwood do a single 60–75 minute tri-region session, or would you prefer a different cadence? We also need the session recorded and a short runbook afterward.

Thanks — suggest a couple of times and we’ll try to align.

— Alex
Alex Carter
Head of Infrastructure, Strata Analytics
alex.carter@strata.ai
+1 415-555-0123
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@strata.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: technical deep-dive with architects across US/EU/APAC

Hi Alex — great to hear. Short answer: we can do a tri-region session but we usually avoid a single long meeting that forces one region into a very inconvenient hour. Instead, I want to propose a "timeband" stitch approach that minimizes jet-lag and gives each region an effective window + a scheduled overlap for cross-region Q&A.

Proposal (two parts):
1) Regional deep dives (45 minutes): US-focused, EU-focused, APAC-focused. Each session is led by the same SE pair but drills into region-specific configs and network constraints.
2) Two 30-minute handshake overlaps: a) US <> EU overlap, and b) US <> APAC overlap. Each handshake is explicitly for architecture Q&A and crosswalks (we record both).

Why this helps: it keeps every architect in a reasonable local hour while giving everyone the ability to hear the same technical answers (via overlap and recordings).

Candidate windows (all times listed with local conversions; note US/EU DST have already ended so values are standard time):
- US <> EU handshake (30 min): 15:00–15:30 UTC — PST 07:00 / EST 10:00 / CET 16:00 / SGT 23:00
- US <> APAC handshake (30 min): 01:00–01:30 UTC — PST 17:00 (previous day) / EST 20:00 / JST 10:00 / SGT 09:00
- Regional deep dives (45 min): schedule immediately before/after a handshake for continuity.

Practical options:
- Option A: Run EU session (CET afternoon) + US<>EU handshake (15:00 UTC) + US session late morning + US<>APAC handshake (01:00 UTC) + APAC session next morning. This stretches across two calendar days but keeps local hours reasonable.
- Option B: Two consecutive days: day 1 EU+handshake, day 2 US+APAC+handshake.

Attachments: Im attaching a quick timeband_matrix_v1.xlsx that maps several candidate dates for next week. I can also generate calendar invites with timezone-safe ICS files once you confirm the preferred option and attendees.

Ask: Which option do you prefer (A/B) and which of these windows are absolute no-go for Sophie or Kenji? If you want a single long session despite the hour mismatch, we can still do that; wed just like to confirm youre okay with the late hour for APAC or early hour for the US.

Thanks — looping Jonas (EU coverage) and Vivek (APAC) to weigh in on load/SE staffing.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Office: (415) 555-0202
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@strata.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@finvera.com>, Kenji Nakamura <kenji.nakamura@zenports.jp>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: technical deep-dive with architects across US/EU/APAC

Thanks Vanessa and team — that makes sense. Sophie and I discussed and we prefer Option A (staggered across two days with the two handshake windows). Sophies constraints: cannot join anything before 09:30 CET and prefers 15:00 CET or later. Kenji (cc'd) says mornings JST are best (09:00–12:00 JST). I (Alex) can do the US<>EU handshake at 10:00 EST (which matches your suggested 15:00 UTC).

If you can draft the invites for Option A with the two handshake slots and attachments (recording + runbook), well confirm internally and accept. Also Kenji, Sophie: if you can reply with absolute no-gos, that helps.

— Alex
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Alex Carter <alex.carter@strata.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 20:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: technical deep-dive with architects across US/EU/APAC

Alex / Vanessa — confirmed on our end that Option A is the least disruptive for the customer and for our SE rota. I updated the attached timeband_matrix_v1.xlsx with two concrete date proposals: 2026-12-07/2026-12-08.

Notes in the sheet:
- We recommend keeping handshake slots to 30 minutes strictly; SEs should prepare a 10-minute top-line and leave 20 minutes for architecture Q&A.
- For recording: use the EU-handshake as the canonical recording for cross-region notes; we will link the US and APAC regional recordings in the follow-up summary.
- Calendar invite creation: create separate invites for each regional deep dive and separate invites for each handshake. In the event invites cross datelines, include explicit UTC times in the description plus local times to avoid confusion (some calendars show odd conversions when users have mobile clients).

Im attaching the edited matrix and will create the invites once you approve the dates.

Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineering (EMEA), Redwood Inference

Subject: Confirmed: Option A dates + invites (please accept)

Alex / Sophie / Kenji — thanks for the quick turn. Weve locked Option A for the proposed dates and created individual calendar invites (links below). Please accept the invites you plan to attend:

- EU regional deep dive (Dec 7): 14:15UTC / CET 15:15. Invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=eu-deepdive-7892
- US<>EU handshake (Dec 7): 15:00UTC / PST 07:00 / EST 10:00. Invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=us-eu-handshake-7892
- US regional deep dive (Dec 8): 16:00UTC / EST 11:00. Invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=us-deepdive-7892
- US<>APAC handshake (Dec 8): 01:00UTC / PST 17:00 (Dec 7) / JST 10:00 / SGT 09:00. Invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=us-apac-handshake-7892
- APAC regional deep dive (Dec 8): 02:00UTC / JST 11:00. Invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=apac-deepdive-7892

Attachments: global_deepdive_invite.ics (timezone-safe ICS bundle); timeband_matrix_v1.xlsx.

Quick notes on DST/calendar edge cases:

- If any participants calendar client shows an off-by-one-hour error, please re-open the invite and look at the UTC row in the description (mobile clients sometimes have cached timezone settings).

Next steps: please accept the specific invites you will attend and Ill add the runbook template (post-call notes + required artifacts). Jonas and Vivek will staff the SEs for the regions indicated.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
